events.summary: Portland, Oregon’s first-ever Pee-wee Pub Crawl, on Saturday, September 26th, 2026, celebrates all things in the Pee-wee Herman/Paul Reubens Universe, but is timed to coincide with the 40th anniversary of the television debut of Pee-wee’s Playhouse, in September 1986, on CBS, where it ran for four glorious years. The Pee-wee Pub Crawl will take place in the Clinton/Division neighborhood of Southeast Portland, from 3-9pm, on Saturday, September 26th. Attendees are encouraged to come in a simple red bow tie and gray suit, or in full regalia, as their favorite Pee-wee Herman Universe character, from Large Marge to Chairry! There will be Pee-wee Universe costume contests, Pee-wee look-alike (“I know you are, but what am I?”) and laugh-alike contests, a Pee-wee’s Playhouse trivia competition, a ‘Tequila’ dance-off, and a cat scavenger hunt! Cat scavenger hunt?! The Pee-wee Pub Crawl is a benefit for PDX Cat Trapper. PDX Cat Trapper is a grassroots, 100% volunteer-driven feral cat rescue group. Not so fun fact: A single unaltered cat and all her offspring having a litter of 4 each over a 10-year period, results in a startling 1,398,101 cats. PDX Cat Trapper is interrupting the alarming feral cat reproductive cycle and humanely supports our area’s community cats. PDX Cat Trapper practices ‘trap-neuter-return,’ and are responsible for hundreds, if not thousands, of community cats getting fixed every year. They also organize cat colony medical care and feeding services though their all-volunteer grassroots outreach program. PDX Cat Trapper is a registered 501(c)(3) charity, and will receive 75% of the proceeds from ticket sales to the PHPC, as well as cash donations collected from the public via donation jars at the participating bars. . PDX Cat Trapper was chosen not only because the organizers of the Pee-wee Pub Crawl are all great cat lovers, but so was Pee-wee Herman! Paul Reubens was a lifelong animal lover, most especially, of cats. When he passed away, he was the loving cat dad of an untouchable feral, Samantha Reuben-Tenderheart, whom he rescued and for whom he built a large catio, when she made it clear she was not to be an indoor cat. Samantha now lives with one of his best friends, who just happens to be the internet’s famous The Kitten Lady! There will be PDX Cat Trapper cash donation jars stationed at each of our bar stops and the public at large will be encouraged to donate to this very worthy cause. The Pee-wee Pub Crawl will be a fun way to spend a Saturday afternoon reconnecting with one of your old Saturday morning favorites, while connecting with other local Pee-wee Herman fans and cat lovers, alike! Pee-wee Pub Crawl participating bars will create their own Pee-wee Herman inspired drink and food specials. Large Marge-aritas and Ice Cream Soup, anyone? The Pee-wee Pub Crawl is the brainchild of the Paul Reubens Pacific Northwest fan club founder, Meredith Walter, and is being organized and led by Jen Lane, of Portland’s beloved BarFly Magazine and BarFly Bar Tours. BarFly conducted dozens of pub crawls for hundreds of guests, every year during its 20 years in the Portland scene (BarFly quickly succumbed to COVID, and ceased operations in 2020). The Pee-wee Pub Crawl will be a chance to recreate, and perhaps even remember, the BarFly Tour experience The Pee-wee Pub Crawl will be held on Saturday, September 26th, 2026, from 3-9pm. All of the bars will be in the Division/Clinton neighborhood. Participants will be traveling between stops on foot or non-motorized wheels (no driving, please!). This will be a 21 and up, only, event. Advance tickets are required, and are available for purchase at https://peeweepubcrawl.com/. 75% of proceeds from ticket sales will be donated to PDX Cat Trapper.
events.title: Pee-wee Pub Crawl - a fundraiser for PDX Cat Trapper

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour

THE EXPERIENCE Join Oscar-nominated production designer Karen Murphy in conversation with interior designer Andee Hess for an evening exploring Murphy's journey from architecture to the world of film. Through behind-the-scenes stories and career reflections, Murphy will share how spaces shape storytelling and reveal the creative process behind designing environments that influence character, emotion, and narrative on screen. This conversation will unpack the powerful relationship between architecture, interiors, and cinematic storytelling, offering a rare glimpse into the art of creating unforgettable worlds. Whether you're passionate about film, design, architecture, or the creative process, this conversation promises inspiration from one of the industry's most accomplished production designers. Want to brush up on Karen's work? Catch THE BRIDE! at a 4 p.m. screening in advance of the talk. ON STAGE: Karen Murphy Karen Murphy is an Australian production designer now based in the United States. Originally trained in architecture, she transitioned to film after working on Baz Luhrmann's Moulin Rouge, which cemented her commitment to the industry. She went on to art direct major films such as The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe, Australia, and The Kite Runner, the latter earning her Art Directors Guild nominations. Murphy has collaborated with Luhrmann and Catherine Martin on films including The Great Gatsby and Elvis, earning recognition from BAFTA, the Art Directors Guild, and the Academy. Her production design credits also include A Star Is Born, Queen & Slim, The Light Between Oceans, Chevalier, and The Order. Recently, she designed Maggie Gyllenhaal's The Bride! and A24's Enemies, which is now in post-production. Karen Murphy's expertise extends beyond film into commercials, interior design, and creative direction, showcasing her versatility in visual storytelling. ON STAGE: Andee Hess Andee Hess is a renowned interior designer known for concept-driven work shaped by a rigorous understanding of material, form, and spatial experience. With a background in welding and a BS in Interior Design, she founded her studio Osmose Design in Portland in 2008. Andee's innovative perspective on spatial design and crafting unique experiences has earned her recognition within the international design community, including features in leading publications. Dubbed "Portland's Secret Design Weapon" by Architectural Digest, Andee's portfolio showcases work for high-profile brands and individuals. Her notable commercial clients include Stumptown, Salt & Straw, and Smith Tea. Andee believes in the transformative power of compelling environments.
events.title: THE DESIGN OF FILM: ANDEE HESS × KAREN MURPHY

events.summary: Glen Hansard, the Irish songwriter, poet, storyteller and bard, was a musician's musician. Most well-known for the Oscar-winning music from the indie film 'Once', including the song Falling Slowly, Glen's imprint on independent folk and rock spread much farther than the night of the Oscars. From street busking, to his Irish rock band The Frames, to his collaboration with Markéta Irglová in the Swell Season, to his solo work that shaped the last two decades of his career, Glen's songwriting had a backbone of honesty that can be hard to find. His dedication to the spirit and mysticism of song inspired thousands of independent artists the world over to find a hopeful, more vulnerable side, and express themselves through whatever artistic means they have. In the wake of his untimely passing on July 29th, 2026 from a motorcycle accident, Glen's positive impact was seen in the outpouring of grief across the world. Portland friends and fans are gathering for a celebration of life and songs for Glen Hansard with a night of song and poetry from some of Portland's favorite local songwriters at the Alberta Rose Theatre. Featured performers include: The Druthers Olivia Awbrey Dan Klee Idea The Artist Rebecca McDade Margaret Wehr Nathan James Earle Chasing Ebenezer Arran Fagan Jacob Miller and more! Whether you're new to Glen's incredible catalogue, familiar with deep cuts from The Frames, or want to sing Falling Slowly in camaraderie with fellow fans, the evening will pay tribute to the arc of Glen's work from beginning to end. Please join us to celebrate the long-lasting music of one of Ireland's \(and Portland's\) most well-loved musicians. Rest In Peace, Glen. Minors ok when accompanied by a parent or guardian. events.summary: George Lopez’s multi-faceted career encompasses television, film, standup comedy, and late-night television. Lopez can be seen in his Netflix original comedy special We’ll Do It For Half which premiered globally over the summer. Last year Lopez was on tour nationwide for his stand-up comedy The Wall World. He also completed his tour for The Comedy Get Down, along with Eddie Griffin, D.L. Hughley, and Cedric the Entertainer. The comedians also debuted their BET scripted comedy series based on the tour. Lopez has been featured in four HBO specials, The Wall in August 2017, It’s Not Me, It’s You in 2012, GRAMMY nominated Best Comedy Album Tall, Dark and Chicano in 2009, and America's Mexican in 2007. Lopez also performed as part of HBO and TBS's Comic Relief 2006. His acclaimed comedy concert, Why You Crying?, debuted on Showtime in 2004. He released his third standup CD, El Mas Chingon, in 2006, which also earned Lopez a GRAMMY nomination in the category of Best Comedy Album. In 2004, he was nominated for a GRAMMY in the same category for his CD Team Leader. He also starred in Lopez on TV Land. Produced by Lopez, the series explored how he struggled between his two worlds and crises that are often of his own making. The half hour single camera serialized comedy aired for two seasons. Lopez Tonight, a late-night television talk show on TBS, also ran for two seasons. It represented Lopez's return to series television after co-creating, writing, producing, and starring in Warner Bros. Television's groundbreaking hit sitcom George Lopez, which ran for six seasons on ABC. George Lopez remains a hit with viewers in syndication on both broadcast stations and cable's Nick at Nite, ranking as one of the top-rated shows on the network and among the top five comedies and top 20 weekly programs in syndication. In film, he was last seen in the crime thriller The Tax Collector with Shia LaBeouf and Lana Parrilla. David Ayer wrote the screenplay and directed the film. He will be next seen in Walking with Herb opposite Edward James Olmos and Mary McDonnell. The faith-based film is inspired by Joe S. Bullock’s novel of the same name. Lopez starred in El Chicano alongside Raúl Castillo, Aimee Garcia, and Emilio Rivera. The film billed as the first Latin superhero movie, premiered at the Los Angeles Film Festival in 2018. In 2015, Lopez was seen in the Lionsgate inspirational drama, Spare Parts. Produced by Lopez, the film is based on a true story about four undocumented Mexican-American teenagers from Phoenix who team up to build an underwater robot that wins the national robotics competition. In 2014, Lopez starred in the multi-camera ensemble comedy Saint George on FX, which he co-created. Lopez also voiced animated characters in a string of animated blockbuster films including Zook in Gnome Alone, Rafael in Rio and Rio 2 along with Jamie Foxx, Anne Hathaway and Jesse Eisenberg, Thurman in Escape from Planet Earth opposite Jane Lynch and Sofia Vergara, Grouchy Smurf in The Smurfs 1 and 2, and The Beverly Hills Chihuahua 1, 2, and 3. His film credits also include the box-office hit Valentine's Day directed by Garry Marshall, River Runs Red, Swing Vote, Henry Poole Is Here and Balls of Fury. In May 2004, Lopez’s autobiography, Why You Crying?, entered The New York Times Bestsellers List top 20. The book was co-written by Emmy winning writer and sportscaster Armen Keteyian. Lopez released his second memoir, I’m Not Gonna Lie And Other Lies You Tell When You Turn 50, in 2013 where he tells the unabashed and hilarious truth about aging – as only he can. Lopez was also the focus of the award-winning documentary Brown is the New Green: George Lopez and the American Dream. In 2006, Lopez received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. In addition, Time named him one of the 25 Most Influential Hispanics in America and the Harris Poll named him one of the Top Ten Favorite Television Personalities. events.summary: Step inside Botticelli’s *Primavera* for an intimate evening of Renaissance music, myth, and philosophy. Guided by Hermes, this performance moves through the spirit of the painting. Our project began from a question at the heart of the Renaissance: what if music, poetry, myth, and philosophy were not separate, but a practice that renews the soul? Inspired by the world of the Florentine Camerata—the musical Academy whose experiments in ancient drama, song, and expressive speech helped give birth to early opera—and by the Neoplatonic revival of Plato, Ficino, Pico, and the ancient theologians, La Primavera explores music as a spiritual and philosophical exercise. Featuring live music, including works by Monteverdi and his contemporaries, La Primavera combines song, projected image, and short philosophical interludes inspired by Plato, Ficino, Pico, Iamblichus, Diotima, Aphrodite, and Eros. These interludes are not lectures, but listening invitations—brief moments that prepare the audience to hear the music and see the painting differently. La Primavera, Palinode's first public performance in Portland, has been developed through a series of workshops that brought together professional musicians and philosophers, drawing upon a form of vital play where philosophy, music, image, myth and live performance come together as a shared ritual of renewal. Come ready to listen, look, and enter the garden. Program Preview Prelude & Philosophical Introduction: Entering the Garden of Remembrance and Renewal Music: Claudio Monteverdi, L’Orfeo Toccata and ritornelli Philosophy: Hermes, Timaeus, Marsilio Ficino I. Winter’s End, Zephyr’s Return: Cloris’s Initiation into the Mysteries of Love Music: Claudio Monteverdi, "Zefiro torna” from L'Orfeo; “Lamento d’Arianna” from L’Arianna Philosophical Interlude: Giovanni Pico della Mirandola II. The Blossoming Spring: Flora’s Abundance Music:, Luzzasco Luzzaschi, “O primavera”; Giovanni Girolamo Kapsberger, Instrumental "canario" Philosophical Interlude: Iamblichus III. The Heat of Summer: The Graces Inspiring Us to Love Music: Barbara Strozzi, “Le tre Gratie à Venere” Philosophical Interlude: Alcibiades IV. Hermes & Diotima’s Call to the Ascension of More Than Apollo Music: Giovanni Girolamo Kapsberger, Toccata seconda arpeggiata; Claudio Monteverdi, “Parch'a lo sdegno” from L’Orfeo Philosophical Interlude: Diotima of Mantinea V. The Ever Fruitful Present: Aphrodite Moves Eros Music: Claudio Monteverdi, “Scendiam, scendiam” from L’incoronazione di Poppea'; “Pur ti miro” from L’incoronazione di Poppea; L’Orfeo ritornello Philosophical Interlude: Diotima of Matinea
events.title: La Primavera: A Night of Renaissance Music, Myth, and Philosophy

The media has called him “...the Tom Robbins of folk music" (The Carbondale Flipside); "Playful, energetic and honest." (The Oregonian); "An unclassifiable and irreverent acoustic performer..." (Austin Chronicle); "One of our leading contemporary songsmiths and music makers" (Victory Music Review); "An adept storyteller ...\[whose\] lyrics run the gamut of personal reflection to commentary on social issues" (Folkwax); "Introspective, satirical, delightfully absurd and always acoustically gentle to the ears..." (Austin Statesman); “Clever. quirky, lyrics that touch on deeper levels of being human...” (Hipfish); "A panoply of anomalous phenomena.” (Jim Larrance, CutUp Sound); and "a melodious punster who brings grins to his listener's lips and vagrant thoughts to their stirred-up minds." events.summary: Written in 1936, this light-hearted comedy has relevance for today in addressing the main theme of finding one’s own way in today’s complex society, while lightly viewing such topics as distrust of government, domestic terrorism and fear of foreign conflicts. “Grandpa” Vanderhof (Robert Lovitz) once worked in the competitive business world. One day, he realized he was unhappy, so he stopped working. Since then, he spends his days catching and raising snakes, watching graduation ceremonies, visiting old friends, and doing whatever else he wants. His daughter Penny (Marilyn Stacey) writes plays simply because a few years ago a typewriter was delivered to the house by accident. His son-in-law Paul Sycamore (Todd Hermanson) spends hours in the basement making illegal fireworks and playing with erector sets. His granddaughter Essie (Bonnie Auguston) sells candy and has been clumsily attempting ballet for over eight years. His grandson-in-law Ed Carmichael (Aiden Brown) plays the xylophone (or tries to) and accidentally distributes Marxist propaganda. Joining this free-for-all are Rheba (Caren Graham), the household cook; her unemployed boyfriend, Donald (Shaun Hennessy); Essie’s opinionated Russian ballet instructor, Mr. Kolenkhov (Mark Schwahn); Olga (Trisha Todd), a Russian Grand Duchess; Gay Wellington (Adrienne Southard), a heavy-drinking actress; Wilbur C. Henderson (Douglas Hout), a forlorn IRS employee; and Mr. De Pinna (Danny Bruno), a deliveryman who arrived 8 years ago and decided to stay. He now helps with the fireworks and dresses in Roman togas to pose for Penny’s portraits. All is somewhat calm until three men from the government (Christopher Sparks, Dan Weiss, and Erik James) visit to investigate Ed’s flyers. In this crazy mix of characters, there is also Alice (Taylor Jean Grady), Penny and Paul’s other daughter and, apparently, the only “normal” family member. She met Tony Kirby (Noah Matthew Rich) at his dad’s Wall Street investment firm, and they’ve fallen in love. Culture shock and fireworks fly when Mr. Kirby (Jeremy Southard) and Mrs. Kirby (Wendy Martel) come to visit. But the message is clear: “Life’s pretty simple if you just relax,” as Grandpa puts it. You Can’t Take It With You is directed by Don Alder. Set design is by Chris Whitten, lighting design is by Demetri Pavlatos, costume design is by Janelle Sutton, prop design is by Allen R. Phillips, the stage manager is Alex Salem, the assistant stage manager is Nat Weinham, and the producer is Steve Knox.
events.title: You Can't Take It With You

events.summary: SEPTEMBER FLIGHT FEATURING 2 SOLOS BY Don Nigro September 11–27 Fri/Sat 7:30, Sun 2 $38 per person Imago Theatre, 17 SE 8th Avenue imagotheatre.com TICKETS https://onthestage.tickets/show/imago-theatre/6a56bc1797fd36b14c05ee83 Tickets also available at the door. Theatre opens one hour before showtime. All seats $38. The show is for mature audiences. The Dark, performed by Joe Cullen (Salomé, Design for Living) and Cincinnati, performed by Diane Slamp (Geography of a Horse Dreamer, Design for Living). Direction by Jerry Mouawad. THE DARK A man in his thirties grapples with a fundamental question: does he truly exist? This dilemma, first encountered at age four, drives the narrative of this ten-page script. Director Jerry Mouawad calls it "the perfect warm-up for Nigro’s work and his intriguing solos, many of which take place in a theatre." CINCINNATI "It’s hard not to feel that this piece was written specifically for Imago," says Slamp, who portrays a lost professor navigating a world of tragedy, sex, and philosophical diatribes. Her diversions reveal a desperate search for redemption amidst personal disaster. "Cincinnati is multi-layered, blending mythology and realism with an ontological examination of life and being," explains Mouawad. "It’s a gem for an audience seeking a new kind of theatre. Don’t let the heavy themes mislead you; this is a small spectacle with humor and high style. I see it as a consciousness tangling with forces of nature, an uncertain reality, and a triad of personas—real or unreal—in a lecture that pushes the boundaries of endurance.” Production Credits: *Light Design:* Ronnie Rantis Costume Design: Laura Helgeson Sound Design: Myrrh Larsen Note: For Mature Audiences In October, Imago returns with October Flight, featuring more solos by Don Nigro.

events.summary: Adapted from Agatha Christie’s classic mystery, this immersive production brings the psychological tension of the classic tale into immediate, breath-held proximity. Our story takes place inside a remote seaside mansion after a violent storm strands ten guests and their hosts. When an eerie accusation recorded on a gramophone accuses each of them of wrongdoing, the guests confront secrets, guilt, and suspicion. Trapped by weather and circumstance, alliances form and fracture… old grievances surface, and rationality gives way to intense fear as each new death raises the stakes. At ETP’s production, you’ll find yourself sitting with the characters within the house itself, among the bedrooms, the dining room, and narrow passages. Experience the shifting power dynamics and mounting claustrophobia as if you were part of the action. Hear whispered confrontations up close, overhear private confessions, and feel the silence before the next crisis. Though the environment surrounds you, the audience is strictly non-participatory — as a silent witness, a “fly on the wall,” you will never be directly addressed by the characters, nor asked to participate. What to expect in performance: \- Tension-driven mystery with tightly controlled pacing and sudden shocks. \- Strong emphasis on atmosphere: storm sound design, flickering lantern and candlelight, thunder, and selective blackout moments. \- Intense emotional scenes: accusations, breakdowns, moral reckonings, and desperate attempts to find the culprit. \- Minimalist, realistic set dressing that transforms the performance space into a lived-in island mansion, with audience seating integrated into set locations (chairs, benches, window alcoves). \- No audience interaction; observers remain silent and stationary throughout each performance. Content warnings: Multiple onstage deaths and depictions of violence (staged, non-graphic). Mature themes and dialogue — recommended for ages 13+ About Experience Theatre Project: Experience Theatre Project is an innovative, immersive theater company based in Aloha, Oregon. Unlike traditional theaters with rows of seats and a proscenium stage, ETP crafts imaginative and fully surrounding narratives, drawing inspiration from both original and classic stories. Our specialty lies in presenting these tales in an unconventional, unexpected fashion, surrounding audiences in the world of the play, similar to a haunted house or a Disney experience. Limiting audiences to sixty or fewer ensures an intimate and memorable experience. Ticket link: www.experiencetheatreproject.org
events.title: ETP Presents Agatha Christie's And Then There Were None

events.summary: TICKETS: truewest.info/Chanel26 Tickets On Sale Friday, May 29th at 10am PT This Event is 21\+ ---------------------------------------- First things first: yes, Chanel Beads’ second album, Your Day Will Come, has the same title as the experimental project’s 2024 breakthrough debut. But this is a completely new body of work, not a “part two,” a rehash or a re-do. If his initial impulse was to poke fun at the apparatus that divides music into chapters, as the songs developed, Shane Lavers found the phrase carried deeper nuance, evoking the duel between certainty and doubt that preoccupied his psyche. Though the phrase unfurls with conviction, a slight shift in emphasis can inspire unsettling ambiguities: Will your day come? What will it be like? How can you be sure? Raised in the suburbs of Minnesota, Lavers began making music under the name Chanel Beads while living in Seattle back in 2016. When he wasn’t working at a library for the blind, he was collaging synthetic sounds and real instruments into beguiling songs fundamentally averse to genre. He was living in New York by 2022, as tracks like “Ef” and “True Altruism” captivated certain online circles with their androgynous vocals, uncanny artifice, and stirring intimacy. In the years since Chanel Beads’ entrancing introduction, the project has gone from playing house shows and illegal abandoned train tunnel shows, all the way up to supporting Lorde on her recent North American arena tour

events.summary: George Lopez’s multi-faceted career encompasses television, film, standup comedy, and late-night television. Lopez can be seen in his Netflix original comedy special We’ll Do It For Half which premiered globally over the summer. Last year Lopez was on tour nationwide for his stand-up comedy The Wall World. He also completed his tour for The Comedy Get Down, along with Eddie Griffin, D.L. Hughley, and Cedric the Entertainer. The comedians also debuted their BET scripted comedy series based on the tour. Lopez has been featured in four HBO specials, The Wall in August 2017, It’s Not Me, It’s You in 2012, GRAMMY nominated Best Comedy Album Tall, Dark and Chicano in 2009, and America's Mexican in 2007. Lopez also performed as part of HBO and TBS's Comic Relief 2006. His acclaimed comedy concert, Why You Crying?, debuted on Showtime in 2004. He released his third standup CD, El Mas Chingon, in 2006, which also earned Lopez a GRAMMY nomination in the category of Best Comedy Album. In 2004, he was nominated for a GRAMMY in the same category for his CD Team Leader. He also starred in Lopez on TV Land. Produced by Lopez, the series explored how he struggled between his two worlds and crises that are often of his own making. The half hour single camera serialized comedy aired for two seasons. Lopez Tonight, a late-night television talk show on TBS, also ran for two seasons. It represented Lopez's return to series television after co-creating, writing, producing, and starring in Warner Bros. Television's groundbreaking hit sitcom George Lopez, which ran for six seasons on ABC. George Lopez remains a hit with viewers in syndication on both broadcast stations and cable's Nick at Nite, ranking as one of the top-rated shows on the network and among the top five comedies and top 20 weekly programs in syndication. In film, he was last seen in the crime thriller The Tax Collector with Shia LaBeouf and Lana Parrilla. David Ayer wrote the screenplay and directed the film. He will be next seen in Walking with Herb opposite Edward James Olmos and Mary McDonnell. The faith-based film is inspired by Joe S. Bullock’s novel of the same name. Lopez starred in El Chicano alongside Raúl Castillo, Aimee Garcia, and Emilio Rivera. The film billed as the first Latin superhero movie, premiered at the Los Angeles Film Festival in 2018. In 2015, Lopez was seen in the Lionsgate inspirational drama, Spare Parts. Produced by Lopez, the film is based on a true story about four undocumented Mexican-American teenagers from Phoenix who team up to build an underwater robot that wins the national robotics competition. In 2014, Lopez starred in the multi-camera ensemble comedy Saint George on FX, which he co-created. Lopez also voiced animated characters in a string of animated blockbuster films including Zook in Gnome Alone, Rafael in Rio and Rio 2 along with Jamie Foxx, Anne Hathaway and Jesse Eisenberg, Thurman in Escape from Planet Earth opposite Jane Lynch and Sofia Vergara, Grouchy Smurf in The Smurfs 1 and 2, and The Beverly Hills Chihuahua 1, 2, and 3. His film credits also include the box-office hit Valentine's Day directed by Garry Marshall, River Runs Red, Swing Vote, Henry Poole Is Here and Balls of Fury. In May 2004, Lopez’s autobiography, Why You Crying?, entered The New York Times Bestsellers List top 20. The book was co-written by Emmy winning writer and sportscaster Armen Keteyian. Lopez released his second memoir, I’m Not Gonna Lie And Other Lies You Tell When You Turn 50, in 2013 where he tells the unabashed and hilarious truth about aging – as only he can. Lopez was also the focus of the award-winning documentary Brown is the New Green: George Lopez and the American Dream. In 2006, Lopez received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. In addition, Time named him one of the 25 Most Influential Hispanics in America and the Harris Poll named him one of the Top Ten Favorite Television Personalities. events.summary: Did you know that 1 in 8 people will be diagnosed with breast cancer in their lifetime? Chances are, you know someone whose life has been touched by this disease. The Support the Girls 5K is more than just a race. It’s a way to stand together, honor survivors, support fighters, and raise funds for free programs that help people affected by breast cancer. If you want to stretch your mind and muscles beyond playing catch with balls and clubs, the festival encourages you to try poi, yoyo, unicycles, hula-hoops, and other props. “We’re very inclusive of toys and people,” says founding Portland Juggler Rhys Thomas. events.summary: Every writer has moments that seem larger than themselves: a night sky, a death, a first encounter with art, a dream, a sentence in a book, a city seen from above, a strange conversation, a childhood image that never stopped working. This one-day workshop helps writers return to one such moment and begin shaping it into literary material. We will discuss a few brief examples of writing that moves from concrete scene to large question. Then participants will work through a guided sequence: re-entering the sensory scene, locating the pivot where perception changed, naming the question the scene still asks, and drafting a short speculative passage that moves between lived detail and wider meaning. This is a generative class rather than a critique workshop. Writers will leave with new pages, a set of prompts for continued work, and a clearer sense of how large ideas can arise from concrete experience. The atmosphere will be supportive, exploratory, and craft-centered: serious play for writers who want to risk wonder without losing the page. Class outcomes Identify one fundamental scene or image that can become literary material. Draft a short speculative passage rooted in sensory detail. Practice moving from scene to question without over-explaining. Learn a simple revision method for deepening image, voice, and structure. Leave with prompts for continuing the piece after class. Access Program We want our writing classes and seminars to be accessible to everyone, regardless of income and background. We understand that our tuition structure can present obstacles for some people. Our Access Program offers writing class and seminar tuitions at a reduced rate. Most writing classes have at least one access spot available. Please apply here for access rate tuition. Contact Susan Moore at susan@literary-arts.org if you have questions. Liaison position Every in-person class and seminar at Literary Arts has one liaison position. Liaisons perform specific duties for each class meeting. If you are a liaison for a class or seminar, the full amount of your tuition is covered by Literary Arts. Apply here for the liaison position.
events.title: Fundamental Scenes: A Speculative Writing Workshop

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Dashing dachshunds, endless sausages, polka, pilsner, pretzels and more will take over Oaks Park Sept. 25-27 during the park’s ever-popular Oktoberfest. The three-day, family-friendly celebration of autumn will be packed with traditional food and beverages, authentic music and dancing and an array of Oktoberfest activities for revelers of all ages. “Over the years, Oaks Park’s Oktoberfest has grown into one of our most popular celebrations of the year,” said Emily MacKay, Oaks Park’s Marketing and Events Director. “From great food and drinks to live music, Bavarian cooking shows, wiener dog races and even a pretzel toss contest, we have something for everyone.” Oaks Park has been hosting its Oktoberfest since the early 1990s. This year’s festival will feature all the favorites that have made the festival at Oaks Park so popular, including: Food and drink: A range of imported Paulaner beers will be available along with craft ciders and wines. Food vendors include Schnitzel Haus, Brat Barn, Wienerwurst, Eis Hutte, the Buffalo Gap and others. Activities: The three-day fest will feature an all-ages dance floor, Bavarian cooking shows, wiener dog races, a pretzel toss, a condiment art contest, a vendor village, a Chicken Dance contest and more. There will also be the kid-friendly Kinderplatz on Saturday and Sunday, where kids can find fun arts, crafts and music. Music: It’s not Oktoberfest without great polka, and Oaks Park has a full lineup, from The Polkatones and The Tirolean Dancers to The Alpine Echoes and accordionist Elizabeth Wisler. In addition to all the Oktoberfest fun, Oaks Park will have its rides, games and other attractions running at full speed. Gate-only admission for Oktoberfest is $7.50 for those 48” and taller and $4.50 for those under 48”. Gate admission with a Ride Bracelet is $44.45 for guests 48” and taller and $23.45 for anyone under 48”. Infants 2 and under are free. Oaks Park’s classic roller-skating rink and mini golf course will also be available for guests for an additional price. Hours for Oktoberfest at Oaks Park are: 4 p.m. to 10 p.m. Friday, Sept. 25; 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. Saturday, Sept. 26; and 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. Sunday, Sept. 27. Video highlights of last year’s Oktoberfest can be seen here. For more information about this year’s Oktoberfest at Oaks Park, including schedules, activity details and more, visit Oakspark.com.

events.summary: Before wine ever touched a glass, it touched human hands and feet. For centuries, harvest wasn’t just about gathering grapes. It was about communities coming together to crush, to laugh, to stain their toes with the first promise of wine. Maryhill keeps that tradition alive. One weekend a year, the barrels are rolled out, the grapes are poured in, and the invitation is simple: step in, stomp down, and be part of the story. This is a rite of passage. The kind of messy, joyous memory you’ll brag about years from now, made even better with your own grape-stained footprints stamped on our “I Got Stomped at Maryhill” T-shirt. Join us for our Annual Grape Stomp & Harvest Party, September 27–28, at all four tasting rooms: Goldendale, Vancouver, Woodinville, Spokane. Not ticketed, but participants pay a $25 fee for a shirt, glass of wine, and to stomp. Come stomp. Come squish. Come sip. And leave with more than a glass of wine. Leave with a harvest story of your own. Because where it’s made matters.

events.summary: The Northwest’s Original Grapestomping is Coming up! Announcing the 44th Annual St JOSEF’S Grapestomping Festival Sept 26th & 27th, 2026 @ St Josef’s Winery- Canby, (Willamette Valley) Oregon German Style Wines, German Music, German Food & even German Beer.... And lots of Grapestomping! Saturday, Sept 26th and Sunday, September 27th. Open Noon – 5pm. Rain or Shine Featuring - The Gordonaires from Canada- a fun band playing German music and more The festival started in 1983 when there were less than 30 wineries in Oregon. Founders, Josef & Lilli who emigrated from Germany, wanted to pass on a little bit of the harvest spirit to the burgeoning Oregon wine industry. Since running a vineyard and winery is a lot of hard work, they believed it was important to start the busy crush season off with a lighthearted approach. A fun harvest festival with lively music, local foods and of course, stomping grapes in a casual European atmosphere! In addition to Grapestomping contests held throughout the day, the ‘Gordonaires’ a great six-piece German Band will be performing from 1pm to 4:30 pm on Saturday and Sunday. Food includes special house recipe German sausages & homemade sauerkraut, along with other locally made foods. New vintages and special reserve wines will be available by the glass, plus tours with the winemaker and tastings will occur throughout the day. Can we stomp the grapes? Yes! We’re always looking for volunteers to help us stomp! This year you can even reserve a spot to with our VIP Grapestomping Packages. Which includes admission for Two, 2 souvenir glasses, wine tasting or a glass of wine or beer for each. Plus a reserved Grapestomping time for two along with tour with the winemaker and three bottles of wine to take home to enjoy (one red, one white, one sparkling from our current releases). We will also be looking for more Grapestomping volunteers throughout the day. (stompers need to be 21+) And everyone will be able to get a picture of their feet in the grapes. Do we need to make a reservation to attend the event? No- but advance tickets will save you 20%. Advance tickets include a souvenir glass and wine tasting (or glass of wine or beer). Tickets at the door will be $15 and include a souvenir glass. Tickets and VIP packages available @ stjosefswinery.com St Josef’s is one of Oregon’s Wine Pioneers with vineyards planted in 1978 and first legal vintage in 1983. 99 % of production is from the property and the 40 acres of estate vineyards have been awarded ‘Salmon Safe’ designation and are tended without the use of irrigation, harsh chemicals or pesticide with goats & llamas helping with the landscaping. The event will feature all of the current releases; selections of reserve wines and sparkling wines – including the latest releases of award winning Lilli Sparkling wines, St Josef’s Chardonnay & Kitara Reserve Syrah. The 44th Annual St Josef’s Grapestomping Festival Hours are noon-5pm both days- Saturday Sept 26th and Sunday 27th 2026. St Josef’s is located at 28836 S Barlow Road, Canby, Oregon. (503) 651-3190 stjosefswinery.com Admission is $15 for those over 21, and includes souvenir wine glass. (Children under 18 are free if supervised, $500 otherwise). Advance admission tickets and VIP stomp packages are available. And bottle discounts for new releases and library reserve wines For more information contact - info@stjosefswinery.com

events.summary: Written in 1936, this light-hearted comedy has relevance for today in addressing the main theme of finding one’s own way in today’s complex society, while lightly viewing such topics as distrust of government, domestic terrorism and fear of foreign conflicts. “Grandpa” Vanderhof (Robert Lovitz) once worked in the competitive business world. One day, he realized he was unhappy, so he stopped working. Since then, he spends his days catching and raising snakes, watching graduation ceremonies, visiting old friends, and doing whatever else he wants. His daughter Penny (Marilyn Stacey) writes plays simply because a few years ago a typewriter was delivered to the house by accident. His son-in-law Paul Sycamore (Todd Hermanson) spends hours in the basement making illegal fireworks and playing with erector sets. His granddaughter Essie (Bonnie Auguston) sells candy and has been clumsily attempting ballet for over eight years. His grandson-in-law Ed Carmichael (Aiden Brown) plays the xylophone (or tries to) and accidentally distributes Marxist propaganda. Joining this free-for-all are Rheba (Caren Graham), the household cook; her unemployed boyfriend, Donald (Shaun Hennessy); Essie’s opinionated Russian ballet instructor, Mr. Kolenkhov (Mark Schwahn); Olga (Trisha Todd), a Russian Grand Duchess; Gay Wellington (Adrienne Southard), a heavy-drinking actress; Wilbur C. Henderson (Douglas Hout), a forlorn IRS employee; and Mr. De Pinna (Danny Bruno), a deliveryman who arrived 8 years ago and decided to stay. He now helps with the fireworks and dresses in Roman togas to pose for Penny’s portraits. All is somewhat calm until three men from the government (Christopher Sparks, Dan Weiss, and Erik James) visit to investigate Ed’s flyers. In this crazy mix of characters, there is also Alice (Taylor Jean Grady), Penny and Paul’s other daughter and, apparently, the only “normal” family member. She met Tony Kirby (Noah Matthew Rich) at his dad’s Wall Street investment firm, and they’ve fallen in love. Culture shock and fireworks fly when Mr. Kirby (Jeremy Southard) and Mrs. Kirby (Wendy Martel) come to visit. But the message is clear: “Life’s pretty simple if you just relax,” as Grandpa puts it. You Can’t Take It With You is directed by Don Alder. Set design is by Chris Whitten, lighting design is by Demetri Pavlatos, costume design is by Janelle Sutton, prop design is by Allen R. Phillips, the stage manager is Alex Salem, the assistant stage manager is Nat Weinham, and the producer is Steve Knox.

Theatre opens one hour before showtime. All seats $38. The show is for mature audiences. The Dark, performed by Joe Cullen (Salomé, Design for Living) and Cincinnati, performed by Diane Slamp (Geography of a Horse Dreamer, Design for Living). Direction by Jerry Mouawad. THE DARK A man in his thirties grapples with a fundamental question: does he truly exist? This dilemma, first encountered at age four, drives the narrative of this ten-page script. Director Jerry Mouawad calls it "the perfect warm-up for Nigro’s work and his intriguing solos, many of which take place in a theatre." CINCINNATI "It’s hard not to feel that this piece was written specifically for Imago," says Slamp, who portrays a lost professor navigating a world of tragedy, sex, and philosophical diatribes. Her diversions reveal a desperate search for redemption amidst personal disaster. "Cincinnati is multi-layered, blending mythology and realism with an ontological examination of life and being," explains Mouawad. "It’s a gem for an audience seeking a new kind of theatre. Don’t let the heavy themes mislead you; this is a small spectacle with humor and high style. I see it as a consciousness tangling with forces of nature, an uncertain reality, and a triad of personas—real or unreal—in a lecture that pushes the boundaries of endurance.” Production Credits: *Light Design:* Ronnie Rantis Costume Design: Laura Helgeson Sound Design: Myrrh Larsen Note: For Mature Audiences In October, Imago returns with October Flight, featuring more solos by Don Nigro.

events.summary: It is not an exaggeration to say The Brothers Karamazov is one of the most influential novels ever written. It is a novel that has a history of dividing opinions, regularly hitting banned book lists: Written in the mid-late 19th century, contemporary Christians believed the novel was atheistic, and contemporary atheists believed the novel is too Christian. Regardless of which it is, the novel is certainly an attempt to tear down established norms and create a blueprint for a new societal order in Russia. Dostoevsky himself spent time in a labor camp earlier in his life, accused of various crimes including fears from the Ministry of Internal Affairs that he was a member of a revolutionary literary group. If Tolstoy’s War and Peace, written a decade earlier, was an attempt to capture the totality of political and interpersonal life, then The Brothers Karamazov is an attempt to capture the totality of internal life. It is a project with no less of a goal than creating a new society and new religion through the demonstration of the tripartite souls of the titular brothers: Aloysha, the exuberant, youthful monk-in-training; Ivan, the depressed, ruminating academic, and Dimitri, the eldest, sensualist, and self-destructive soldier. Each character represents a period of life and a way of looking at the world; though archetypes, they also feel like people you may have known. When their miserable and cruel estranged father is murdered, all three have to face his self-destructive aspects in themselves: Why are modern humans miserable when we know we could be happy, and why can’t we seem to get out of our own way? And who among Fyodor Zaramazov’s orbit killed him, and why? We will be reading the Peaver and Volokhonsky translation, itself a major turning point in the novel’s popularity in English, shedding some of the stuffy, plodding, confusing language of earlier translations in favor a readable and populist style. The Brothers Karamazov is a big novel full of big ideas, and there is no better way to experience it than in a group. Required Texts: The Brothers Karamazov, Bicentennial Edition, trans. Peaver and Volokhonsky Reading schedule: Week 1: 1-173 \(Part I\) Week 2: 173-300 \(Part II, Books 4-5\) Week 3: 300-472 \(Part II, Book 6 – Part III, Books 7-8\) Week 4: 472- 545 \(Part III, Book 9\) Week 5: 545- 696 \(Part IV, Books 10-11\) Week 6: 696-825 \(Part IV Book 12 & Epilogue\) Access Program We want our writing classes and seminars to be accessible to everyone, regardless of income and background. We understand that our tuition structure can present obstacles for some people. Our Access Program offers writing class and seminar tuitions at a reduced rate. Most writing classes have at least one access spot available. Please apply here for access rate tuition. Contact Susan Moore at susan@literary-arts.org if you have questions. Liaison position Every in-person class and seminar at Literary Arts has one liaison position. Liaisons perform specific duties for each class meeting. If you are a liaison for a class or seminar, the full amount of your tuition is covered by Literary Arts. Apply here for the liaison position.

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour

events.summary: Internationally acclaimed guitarist, composer and producer Chance Hayden presents the Desert Room All Stars, a monthly series every Last Sunday \(September-April\) at McMenamins Al’s Den evoking the venue’s mid-century history as the Desert Room, featuring rotating guest artists performing golden era jazz and blues! There is little doubt that jazz guitar has entered a new and exciting realm when Dan Faehnle takes the stage. With the technical prowess of a jazz giant, Ohio native Faehnle has made an indelible mark upon the music world, receiving high praise from audiences and critics alike. From an up-tempo bebop anthem to a languid, emotional reading of a ballad, Faehnle’s nimble fingers caress his guitar. Beginning in 2000, Faehnle stepped into the guitar chair with Diana Krall, performing on numerous world tours, television shows, radio and media events. As an integral part of the Diana Krall quartet for three years, Dan garnered accolades from such publications as the New York Times, Los Angeles Times, JazzTimes and Downbeat magazines, as well as many international publications. While based in Portland, Oregon, Dan established relationships with such legendary jazz artists as Leroy Vinnegar, Chuck Israels, Dave Frishberg, Mel Brown, Ron Steen, Nancy King, David Friesen, Rebecca Kilgore and Dick Berk. Faehnle has also worked with such noted musicians as Joey DeFrancesco, Eddie Harris, Clark Terry, Zoot Sims, Jeff Hamilton and he is an original member of one of Portland's most widely known acts: Pink Martini.

events.summary: The lore of Cain Culto is layered and complex. A former worship pastor-turned-queer renegade with a story of contradiction and evolution, his provocative take on left-field pop and hip-hop with global influences is unlike any other. A DIY auteur, Culto develops bold, uncompromising music and visuals that pull at the threads of faith, politics, race, and capitalism in the form of wild-eyed, original pop music. The name ‘Cain Culto’ refers to the shadowy, fratricidal Old Testament character of Cain, and the Spanish word for worship ‘Culto’. Born in Florida, Andrew Padilla was raised in a Colombian and Nicaraguan household, listening to salsa and cumbia. At the age of 5, his family moved to Kentucky, where he learned bluegrass fiddle and attended a fundamentalist evangelical church. Culto spent his youth hiding his queerness, trying to conform with his surroundings - a familiar tale of religious trauma many queer people experience - ultimately leading to a breakdown, and hospitalization in 2021. He ended his acclaimed Christian band ‘Ecclesia’ and broke from the church, reemerging as Cain Culto. The Culto persona represents a realignment with spirituality, sexuality, and cultural heritage. The ethos is built around challenging dogma, knowing oneself, and protecting freedom of thought. Dedicated to making some of the boldest, and most fearless alternative music around, Culto brings together high and low art, political protest, satire, controversy, and undeniable pop magic as an antidote to mass-produced music culture. A skilled singer, rapper, producer, and visual artist, Culto has the skills to realize his ambitious vision, performing a suite of instruments across his songs, self-styling, and directing his music videos.
events.title: Cain Culto

events.summary: K&D are two producers/djs/remixers whose distinctive trademark sound is at most times extremely mellow, has a lot of bass, downbeat tracks and a sense of epic soundscapes. There might be the occasional double-time breaks and the heavy and deep typically viennese feeling. Consider K&D to roam in their own, unique realm of musical beutekunst that owes and gives a lot to rare funk tunes, electric jazz arrangements, the feeling of deep soul, hiphop, dub, reggae, ambient, fusion, brazil, chansons, dope beats and drum\+bass and still a lot more influences that happen to find the interest of the two austrians. At a time when hip hopbeats started to emancipate themselves from the rapping and everyone started to pay highest attention to the blooming breakbeat scene in the UK, K&D broke through out of nowhere with one 4-track e.p. \(G-stoned\) that featured a hypnotic track called High Noon and a cover that showed the dj-duo in true Simon & Garfunkel form, straight out of Richard Avedon anno 1969. The impact was massive, especially since the first wave of enthusiasm came from the UK where musical imports from the continent are seldom appreciated. Gilles Peterson played the track at first on his famous now called Worldwide-show. Gathering momentum with support from people like Wall of Sounds Mark Jones and tracks for fellow Austrians Count Basic or strange people like William Orbit, the further story of K&D and Richard's Tosca project is well documented on various compilations and twelve inch releases. They met people like the Ninja tune posse, touched base with the leftfield dance, befriended Munich's Compost crew, remixed artists as diverse as Bomb the bass, Bones thugs & harmony, Alex Reece, United Future Organisation, Rockers Hifi \(the K&D version was used in the video of "Going under"\), Lamb, Roni Size, Depeche Mode and dj-ed in more clubs than you would care to count. Be it their self-produced tracks or the sound of their remixes, the K&D symptomatic feeling of lush european loungcore-dub pervaded all swift changes of the triphop hype and survived as a highly personal expression that found easy access into the world of drum&bass when the breakbeats became soulful. Their regular presence in the club circuit, a characteristic side effect of their consistant travelling as djs, made them well-received guest at the various crossing of an international beat-set that took them from Vienna to London, to the American Westcoast, to Germany and back, with a tightly packed dj-bag full of remixes tracing their steps. A mix-CD compilation, DJ-kicks, for german label studio K7 marked a relevant change in the overall concept of K&D or rather in the way the audience seemed to take them in. From being well-respected underground heroes they had emerged to be full fledged media-celebrities in the music-press whose mix-CD was so excellently mixed and selected, that many new fans were attracted all over the world. K&D are maybe something like the continental answer to the british breakbeat or the american illbient scene, but then again their musical imprint is outernational anyway. They could achieve the special abstract global reputation that makes them neighbours to RockersHifi, Fila Brazilia, Howie B., DJ Shadow, the wordsound collective, Coldcut or the Thievery corporation in a virtual neighbourhood of twekwando-ing beatmeisters. But, with a number of prolific dj-dates of K&D all around the world and the production and releases of Tosca and Peace Orchestra as well as numerous remixes, it seems unavoidable that there will be a lot of talk about Peter Kruder & Richard Dorfmeister.
events.title: Kruder & Dorfmeister

events.summary: Adapted from Agatha Christie’s classic mystery, this immersive production brings the psychological tension of the classic tale into immediate, breath-held proximity. Our story takes place inside a remote seaside mansion after a violent storm strands ten guests and their hosts. When an eerie accusation recorded on a gramophone accuses each of them of wrongdoing, the guests confront secrets, guilt, and suspicion. Trapped by weather and circumstance, alliances form and fracture… old grievances surface, and rationality gives way to intense fear as each new death raises the stakes. At ETP’s production, you’ll find yourself sitting with the characters within the house itself, among the bedrooms, the dining room, and narrow passages. Experience the shifting power dynamics and mounting claustrophobia as if you were part of the action. Hear whispered confrontations up close, overhear private confessions, and feel the silence before the next crisis. Though the environment surrounds you, the audience is strictly non-participatory — as a silent witness, a “fly on the wall,” you will never be directly addressed by the characters, nor asked to participate. What to expect in performance: \- Tension-driven mystery with tightly controlled pacing and sudden shocks. \- Strong emphasis on atmosphere: storm sound design, flickering lantern and candlelight, thunder, and selective blackout moments. \- Intense emotional scenes: accusations, breakdowns, moral reckonings, and desperate attempts to find the culprit. \- Minimalist, realistic set dressing that transforms the performance space into a lived-in island mansion, with audience seating integrated into set locations (chairs, benches, window alcoves). \- No audience interaction; observers remain silent and stationary throughout each performance. Content warnings: Multiple onstage deaths and depictions of violence (staged, non-graphic). Mature themes and dialogue — recommended for ages 13+ About Experience Theatre Project: Experience Theatre Project is an innovative, immersive theater company based in Aloha, Oregon. Unlike traditional theaters with rows of seats and a proscenium stage, ETP crafts imaginative and fully surrounding narratives, drawing inspiration from both original and classic stories. Our specialty lies in presenting these tales in an unconventional, unexpected fashion, surrounding audiences in the world of the play, similar to a haunted house or a Disney experience. Limiting audiences to sixty or fewer ensures an intimate and memorable experience. Ticket link: www.experiencetheatreproject.org
events.title: ETP Presents Agatha Christie's And Then There Were None

events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) presents A Good Universe Next Door – A redacted past, a precarious present, and an uncertain future, a group exhibition curated by Celeste Noche and Melanie Stevens. On view in the Front & Center Galleries from September 18 through October 17, 2026, the exhibition features new work by four regional artists: Amber Capwell, Ebony Frison, Maryanna Hollomon, and Orlando Almanza. An opening reception will be held Saturday, September 19, from 1–3 p.m., and an artist talk will take place Saturday, October 10 at 2 p.m. Stevens and Noche invited the artists to consider how utopia and dystopia manifest in their lives, and how they interpret these experiences. Through sculpture, photography, printmaking, and painting, the artists offer visions of futures shaped by remembrance, resistance, solidarity, creativity, and care. Ebony Frison approaches utopia and dystopia as “conditions that coexist within the same historical moment.” Working with archival research, printmaking, photography, and artist books, Frison examines how Black histories persist despite erasure, describing utopia as “a practice of rememory—an active engagement with ancestral knowledge, community care, and historical reclamation.” Maryanna Hollomon highlights the aftermath of war for children and the global systems that produce displacement. “A utopia cannot be achieved without working in solidarity with those most oppressed,” she writes. Her work asks viewers to consider militarism’s impact and to imagine new forms of resistance and collective care. Amber Capwell creates sculptural works that envision utopian possibilities through Tarot readings for endangered Pacific Northwest flora and fauna. “These sculptures exist as a reminder to care,” they write. Their work incorporates queer and trans identities as part of an ecological futurism that demands “a utopia existing where we are allowed to live and thrive.” Orlando Almanza imagines futures built on safety, connection, and community. “I dream of a place where my people can have picnics next to the river, to rest, to laugh… and the grandmothers can enjoy their old age, sitting in their rocking chairs on their front porch,” he writes. “Sueño con el día que pueda ver a mi familia reunida, en la tierra que nos vio nacer” (I dream that one day my family can be reunited, in the land that birthed us). The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. It is open Monday – Thursday 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Friday – Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Additional Information: The Multnomah Arts Center is a part of Portland Parks & Recreation. MAC offers programs in a wide range of visual, music, movement, theater, and literary arts at an affordable cost to people of all ages. In addition to this vibrant arts education program, MAC runs a community-based visual arts exhibition program, which includes the MAC Front & Center Galleries. MAC also hosts theatre, music and dance performances, and other special events. The Multnomah Arts Center Association (MACA) is an all-volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that exists to support equity and access to arts education at MAC. MACA provides scholarships, supports community engagements efforts, and provides specialized arts equipment and facility improvements. Their efforts expand opportunities and enhance the experience of students, instructors, and the community at-large. events.summary: This class will provide practical insights and techniques to craft short stories that captivate and create an emotional resonance with readers. We will explore the practice of writing fiction as an experience that not only includes putting words to page, but also as an act of listening, observing, and paying attention. We shall explore what makes a compelling short story by thinking through how to write a powerful opening/create a strong hook, establishing stakes in a story, making the best narrative choices, and achieving a powerful ending/resolution. Throughout the course, we’ll discuss important craft elements, including the plot, characterization, setting, and point of view, amongst others. Our work will be guided by readings of diverse contemporary authors and discussions of core craft elements, as well as writing exercises and workshops. We’ll explore what it means to articulate and be challenged by language, and to reconstruct closeness with language. Class Outcomes ● Define and identify core elements of fiction, including character/characterization, dialogue, points of view, setting, time, narrative structure, and tone. ● Use these elements intentionally in the class’s written work. ● Provide generative feedback to others and revise own work. Readings: Short stories by diverse authors from across the world will be provided. Access Program We want our writing classes and seminars to be accessible to everyone, regardless of income and background. events.summary: The Multnomah Arts Center (MAC) presents A Good Universe Next Door – A redacted past, a precarious present, and an uncertain future, a group exhibition curated by Celeste Noche and Melanie Stevens. On view in the Front & Center Galleries from September 18 through October 17, 2026, the exhibition features new work by four regional artists: Amber Capwell, Ebony Frison, Maryanna Hollomon, and Orlando Almanza. An opening reception will be held Saturday, September 19, from 1–3 p.m., and an artist talk will take place Saturday, October 10 at 2 p.m. Stevens and Noche invited the artists to consider how utopia and dystopia manifest in their lives, and how they interpret these experiences. Through sculpture, photography, printmaking, and painting, the artists offer visions of futures shaped by remembrance, resistance, solidarity, creativity, and care. Ebony Frison approaches utopia and dystopia as “conditions that coexist within the same historical moment.” Working with archival research, printmaking, photography, and artist books, Frison examines how Black histories persist despite erasure, describing utopia as “a practice of rememory—an active engagement with ancestral knowledge, community care, and historical reclamation.” Maryanna Hollomon highlights the aftermath of war for children and the global systems that produce displacement. “A utopia cannot be achieved without working in solidarity with those most oppressed,” she writes. Her work asks viewers to consider militarism’s impact and to imagine new forms of resistance and collective care. Amber Capwell creates sculptural works that envision utopian possibilities through Tarot readings for endangered Pacific Northwest flora and fauna. “These sculptures exist as a reminder to care,” they write. Their work incorporates queer and trans identities as part of an ecological futurism that demands “a utopia existing where we are allowed to live and thrive.” Orlando Almanza imagines futures built on safety, connection, and community. “I dream of a place where my people can have picnics next to the river, to rest, to laugh… and the grandmothers can enjoy their old age, sitting in their rocking chairs on their front porch,” he writes. “Sueño con el día que pueda ver a mi familia reunida, en la tierra que nos vio nacer” (I dream that one day my family can be reunited, in the land that birthed us). The Multnomah Arts Center is located at 7688 SW Capitol Hwy, Portland, OR, 97219. It is open Monday – Thursday 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Friday – Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Additional Information: The Multnomah Arts Center is a part of Portland Parks & Recreation. MAC offers programs in a wide range of visual, music, movement, theater, and literary arts at an affordable cost to people of all ages. In addition to this vibrant arts education program, MAC runs a community-based visual arts exhibition program, which includes the MAC Front & Center Galleries. MAC also hosts theatre, music and dance performances, and other special events. The Multnomah Arts Center Association (MACA) is an all-volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that exists to support equity and access to arts education at MAC. MACA provides scholarships, supports community engagements efforts, and provides specialized arts equipment and facility improvements. Their efforts expand opportunities and enhance the experience of students, instructors, and the community at-large. For more information about MAC or MACA, please call 503.823.2787 or visit www.multnomahartscenter.org.

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Close reading is a practice of attention: an antidote to speed and frictionless swipability. It helps us appreciate literature more deeply and shapes us into more deft practitioners of craft. Paisley Rekdal notes, “When we take the same critical care with our own writing that we take with published poems, we are bound not only to see the patterns behind our failings, but \(more important\) new and more adventurous paths open up in the ways we represent our worlds.” In this generative class we will close-read—and write—alongside works that resist easy classification, including “Everyday Barf” by Eileen Myles, “Dead Doe” by Brigit Pegeen Kelly, “Exhausting a Place in Paris” by Georges Perec, Christina Sharpe’s “The Shapes of Grief,” and Rekdal’s “Nightingale: A Gloss.” Writers will come away with sharpened tools of observation, tactile craft practices, a portfolio of fresh writing starts, and a keener sense of the uncommon and the poetic within the everyday—on and off the page. Access Program Our Access Program offers writing class and seminar tuitions at a reduced rate. Most writing classes have at least one access spot available. Please apply here for access rate tuition. Contact Susan Moore at susan@literary-arts.org if you have questions.
events.title: Extra/Ordinary: Writing the Uncommon in the Everyday

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour
events.title: Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness - Inaugural Concert Season
